lessons.title: Your Radial Menu
lessons.summary: Open your tools right where you are drawing.

steps.title: Open the Radial Menu
steps.text: Tap the touch puck to open the radial menu. With Apple Pencil Pro, you can squeeze instead.

steps.title: Everything Within Reach
steps.text: Drag the arcs to change size and other settings, or tap a tool in the centre. Tap the page when you are finished.

steps.title: Make It Yours
steps.text: Preferences > Radial Menu lets you choose what it shows, how large it is and which tools stay on it.
steps.opened: Radial Menu in this list sets what it shows, how large it is and which tools stay on it. Finish closes Preferences.

lessons.title: Choose a Background
lessons.summary: Keep the page plain or add a living background.

steps.title: Plain by Default
steps.text: New installs start plain, so the app stays quick on every iPad. Open Preferences, then Background, to choose a living background.
steps.opened: Choose Background in this list to pick a living background. Finish closes Preferences.

lessons.title: Add Bismuth Widgets
lessons.summary: Keep your drawings and a daily idea on your Home Screen.

steps.title: Add a Widget
steps.text: On your Home Screen, hold an empty spot, tap Edit, then Add Widget, and choose Bismuth Studio.

steps.title: Pick What Helps
steps.text: Recent Drawings reopens your work. Quick Start begins a new drawing. Daily Pattern offers a new symmetry idea each day.

steps.title: Private on the Lock Screen
steps.text: Drawing names and pictures on Recent Drawings are hidden while your iPad is locked.

lessons.title: Draw in Symmetry
lessons.summary: Turn one line into a balanced pattern.

steps.title: Choose Your Segments
steps.text: Rotate repeats each line around the centre. Use minus and plus to change how many copies you get.

steps.title: Add a Mirror
steps.text: Mirror reflects every line as well, for a perfectly balanced pattern.

steps.title: Try It
steps.text: Draw one line on the page and watch every copy appear.

lessons.title: Clean Joins
lessons.summary: Tidy the small overshoot where lines meet.

steps.title: Draw a Line
steps.text: Clean Joins is on for this lesson. Draw one line on the page.

steps.title: Cross It
steps.text: Draw another line that runs just past the first. The small overshoot is trimmed for you.

steps.title: Find the Switch
steps.text: Open the radial menu from the touch puck whenever you want to switch Clean Joins on or off.

lessons.title: Trim Loose Ends
lessons.summary: Cut a line back to the nearest crossing.

steps.title: Make a Crossing
steps.text: Draw two lines that cross, leaving a loose end past the crossing.

steps.title: Pick Trim
steps.text: Trim shares this button with the eraser. It is selected for you now.

steps.title: Cut It Back
steps.text: Scribble across the loose end. It cuts back to the nearest crossing.

lessons.title: Steady Your Lines
lessons.summary: Use Smoothing and the rope to calm a shaky hand.

steps.title: Open the Radial Menu
steps.text: Tap the touch puck. Smoothing, Clean Joins, Pressure and the Rope Stabiliser are the small switches on the ring.

steps.title: Hold for Settings
steps.text: Tap a switch to turn it on or off. Hold it to open the settings for that one control. Tap the page when you are finished.

steps.title: Try It
steps.text: Draw a slow, wavy line and see how it settles.

lessons.title: Fill a Shape with Small Gaps
lessons.summary: Fill closes tiny openings in a line for you.

steps.title: Draw a Shape
steps.text: Draw a closed shape on the page. A tiny gap where the ends meet is fine.

steps.title: Fill It
steps.text: Tap inside the shape. If a small gap would let the colour escape, Fill closes it and tells you.

steps.title: Larger Gaps
steps.text: For a wider opening, drag the Gap control on the left toolbar upward, then tap again.

lessons.title: Clip a Pattern to a Shape
lessons.summary: Keep a pattern inside the shape below it.

steps.title: Draw the Shape
steps.text: Draw a closed shape for your pattern to stay inside.

steps.title: Fill It
steps.text: Tap inside the shape to fill it. A clipped layer only shows where this layer has ink.

steps.title: Add a Layer
steps.text: Add a new layer for the pattern.

steps.title: Switch On Clip
steps.text: Tap Clip so this layer only shows where the layer below has ink.

steps.title: Draw the Pattern
steps.text: Draw across the shape in the new colour. Anything outside it stays hidden.

steps.title: Print What You See
steps.text: Open Print Stencil. It follows your clipped layers, so the stencil matches the page.
steps.opened: The preview shows only what the clip keeps. Dotted lines are one of the line styles you can print. Finish closes this panel.

lessons.title: Cut Out with a Mask
lessons.summary: Show or hide part of the layer below.

steps.title: Draw the Pattern
steps.text: Draw the pattern you want to cut.

steps.title: Add a Layer
steps.text: Add a new layer for the mask.

steps.title: Choose the Mask
steps.text: Tap Mask to show the pattern inside your mask. Tap again to hide it there instead.

steps.title: Draw the Mask
steps.text: Draw over the pattern. Only the parts under your mask stay visible, and the mask itself never prints.

lessons.title: Print a Stencil
lessons.summary: Size a design for skin and print it.

steps.title: Open Print Stencil
steps.text: When your design is ready, Print Stencil prepares it for skin.
steps.opened: Tap Next for the settings that matter most.

steps.title: Set It Up
steps.text: Set the width on skin, switch on Mirror for Transfer if you need it, and check the preview before printing.

lessons.title: Send Feedback as You Test
lessons.summary: Mark up the screen and dictate notes.

steps.title: Start Feedback Mode
steps.text: Tap the speech bubble on the right-hand toolbar. A small bar stays on screen while you test, and glows until you tap Stop.

steps.title: Add a Note
steps.text: Tap Add Note and mark up the screenshot. Your artwork is hidden unless you choose to include it. Words are optional, and you can tap a saved note to change it later.

steps.title: Send When Ready
steps.text: Review your notes and send them together. Claude reads them only if you switch that on.

knownIssues.title: Undo With the Pen Tools
knownIssues.detail: Undo can behave unexpectedly after drawing with the pen tools.

knownIssues.title: Feedback Screenshots Can Show Your Artwork
knownIssues.detail: Screenshots taken in Feedback Mode show whatever is on screen, including your artwork.
knownIssues.workaround: Use Cover to hide anything private before saving a note. A coming update hides artwork automatically.

knownIssues.title: SVG and PDF Export Ignore Masks and Clipping
knownIssues.detail: Masked or clipped layers export as if the mask or clip were not there. The app warns you when this applies.
knownIssues.workaround: Export a PNG, or use Print Stencil, which follows masks and clipping.

knownIssues.title: Masks Can Look Confusing in Print Stencil
knownIssues.detail: Masks can show unexpected marks in the Print Stencil preview. A full review of masks is planned.
knownIssues.workaround: Clipping works as expected and can often be used instead.

knownIssues.title: The Eraser Leaves Rounded Ends
knownIssues.detail: Erasing part of a line leaves rounded ends instead of a clean cut.
knownIssues.workaround: Trim cuts lines back to a crossing with clean ends.

knownIssues.title: Live Trace Can Miss Parts of a Picture
knownIssues.detail: Live Trace, an experimental tool, can leave some areas of a photo untraced.
knownIssues.workaround: Adjust the trace settings, or trace the missing parts by hand.

knownIssues.title: Restore Purchase in Test Builds
knownIssues.detail: Purchases cannot be restored in TestFlight builds. Everything is already open for testers.
